concept:
« Le trait » (The stroke), final cut, amended by the owner on 2026-10-18 (A1, people and pictures: the hook opens on a picture of a salon owner at her paper notebook, and a people beat closes the answers before the end card; A2, the salon page: the public page opens on Maison Nala's own cover photo and logo; see `amendments`). One white stroke, drawn with the single weight and round caps of the MyWeli mark, crosses out three things that go wrong on a salon day in Abidjan:
1. the paper appointment book (« carnet ») a salon owner is writing in;
2. the same client questions arriving at 22:41;
3. a client who walks in without an appointment and has to be squeezed between two lines, with no number.

Each pain is shown in black: a hard cut in, things popping on `fast`. Each ends with the stroke crossing the whole frame, then thickening into a clean paper page (#FAFAFA). On that page MyWeli Pro answers with real footage of the demo salon « Maison Nala »:
- « Ma journée » with the « Arrivé » swipe;
- the public salon page (its cover photo and logo, tariffs, map, hours — A2);
- a booking added from « Libre — 14:45 » for a client without a number, ending on « Rendez-vous créé ».

The first time the stroke becomes paper, a pen dot draws the MyWeli mark. « MyWeli Pro » and the approved Pro line « Plus de clients, moins de gestion. » sit beside it, so the brand and the promise land between 2.7 and 3.5 s. After the last answer, a stylist braiding a relaxed client says what the answers give back: « Plus de temps pour votre métier. » Then the mark draws itself again and becomes the real Pro app icon, above a black pill reading « Disponible sur l’App Store ».

Pains are black, abrupt and staccato. Answers are paper, smooth and decelerating. That contrast carries the story with the sound off.

Every strike and « trait » starts at a short visible length (four times its width) and grows left to right: never a lone dot.

Spec: 1080×1920, 30 fps, 900 frames, H.264 High@4.1, no music (silent stereo AAC 48 kHz track only). Every cut sits on a 0.5 s grid (frames 75, 180, 300, 375, 525, 600, 810) except one: the S7 → S7b dissolve starts at frame 731 (24.37 s, R2), so S7b's caption has the reading time its 32 characters need. It is a 200-ms dissolve, not a hard cut, and its middle (24.45 s) falls within 2 frames of the 24.5 s beat. A track the owner adds at 115–130 BPM can lock to the grid.

Shared answer layout (S3, S5, S7):
- Paper #FAFAFA. The headline is Poppins Medium 84/96 px, #1A1A1A, centred in the column x 90–990, with the block at y 316–508. S5's is set at 78 px (A2: its first line, « Photos, tarifs, horaires : », is 965 px at 84).
- A header band of paper covers y 0–552, then fades to transparent over y 552–600. It sits above the card, so the card slides under it.
- The card enters the same way in every answer: the card as it rests, clipped by the band, rises 1320 px from y 1920 on `emphasis` (never more than 410 px in a frame). The card and its shadow are laid as one group under the band's fade, so the shadow never shows through the fading card.
- The card is the capture cropped from screen point 56 down, so the 09:41 status bar and the recorder's Dynamic Island never show. It is 900 px wide at x 90–990: scale 0.7463, which is 2.2388 px per pt. Radius 110, 3 px #D0D0D0 ring, the stills' shadows scaled to 1080 (0.10/blur 37/dy 25 and 0.05/blur 15/dy 10), 2× supersampled.
- A camera window W (in screen points) places a screen point p at frame y = 600 + (p − W) × 2.2388 and x = 90 + pt × 2.2388.
- Every UI row position below was measured on frames grabbed at zero tolerance from the takes. The pt-ruled sheets are /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sadreddinedaher-beauty-app/58216b90-3f74-471a-bb6c-3d7031508e23/scratchpad/final-sb/s1.png and s2.png.
hook:
0.00–2.50 s. Amended by the owner on 2026-10-18 (A1): the owner's picture replaces the drawn notebook.

**Frame 0** is already a complete, high-contrast picture:
- A salon owner writing appointments in a paper notebook at her counter: the owner's picture (AI-generated, illustrative, never presented as a real person), full bleed, darkened at the top by a black gradient.
- Over it, the white question « Votre salon, / encore au carnet ? » in Poppins Medium 92 px at y 280–492, at the top of the safe zone (R2: its second line clears her hairline). It names the audience and the pain in 5 words.

**Motion starts at once:**
- The headline settles from scale 1.02 over frames 0–3.
- The picture pushes in slowly toward the notebook: 1.00 → 1.04 over 2.5 s.
- At 1.45 s a white stroke leaves her pen and crosses out the page she is writing, above the Reels caption zone.

**Why it stops the scroll:**
- A person and her own notebook, in a feed of products: a salon owner recognises the scene before reading a word.
- The question is readable at frame 0 and stays on screen until the paper covers it, about 2.77 s, against the 2.57 s that 31 characters need.

**Hand-off.** At 2.50 s the stroke thickens into the white page on which the mark draws itself (2.80 s), with the promise beside it at 3.20 s. The brand and the main message are both in before 3.5 s.

**Cover.** The cover is frame 54 (1.80 s): the picture, the headline and the stroke across the notebook. Everything sits inside the 4:5 feed crop (y 285–1635) and the 3:4 grid crop (y 240–1680), and the headline reads at grid-thumbnail size.

« Tarifs » on the public page is the collapsed line « 5 services • Voir les tarifs ». The prices are one tap away: provider_detail_screen.dart expands to every _ServiceTile with its price. The claim is true but not shown literally. A take with Services opened would show it.

« En quelques gestes » sits on a declared dissolve that hides 97 s of scripted input: one service tick, the checkbox, typing a six-character name and a scroll. It is approved store copy and the App Store film's cut; it is now 12 frames on `slow` with a clean picture on each side, so it reads as a time skip, never as a speed-up.

« Plus de clients » is an outcome promise with no number. It rests on the public page bringing bookings once a salon is live, and the take's own button says « Réserver (après la mise en ligne) ». Post only when salons can actually be published and booked by clients, and only after the App Store release.

The CTA is App Store only (the owner's decision, flagged only). Most owners in Côte d'Ivoire use Android and get no install path. It is a text CTA: Apple's badge would mean downloading Apple's artwork, and the wording « Télécharger dans l’App Store » differs from the fixed line.

Logo: no official « MyWeli Pro » lockup file exists. The wordmark unit is assembled from the wordmark SVG plus the « Pro » vectors inside the Pro app-open Lottie. The end card's mark-becomes-icon move is a new arrangement. Both need the owner's sign-off, because the brand forbids re-spaced or typed logos.

Register and wording: « Votre salon, encore au carnet ? », the four client messages, and « carnet » versus « cahier » were chosen without a sourced local reference. A local reader should validate them; Nouchi is avoided. The white strikes over pain text and the hard cuts to black are brand-review points against 'Calm, not hyped'. They are graphic strokes in the mark's language, not underlines, and abruptness is kept for the two pain cuts (10.0 s and 17.5 s). The other three transitions are smooth paper fills.

S2 holds the lockup and tagline for 2.5 s, from 3.50 to 6.00 s. That is the slowest stretch of the film, and the price of letting the 34-character promise be read in full. If tests show viewers swiping away there, the fallback is a 2.0 s S2 without the tagline, with the line moved into the post caption.

whyThisOne:
Both judges picked « Le trait » (marketing 8 against 7 and 6.5; truth, feasibility and brand 8.3 against 7.4 and 5.9), and the fixes made it stronger.

**For you, in plain terms:**
- It stops the scroll with your customers' own problem: the paper notebook, the same questions at night, the client who walks in without an appointment.
- It answers each problem straight away with a real screen of MyWeli Pro.
- It reads fully with the sound off, it keeps your calm black-and-white brand, and it promises nothing the app does not do: no reminders, no payment, no deposit, no invented numbers.

**Changes from the judged version:**
- The no-show beat is replaced by the walk-in booking, which the app fully answers on real footage.
- Your Pro line « Plus de clients, moins de gestion. » now appears next to the logo in the first 4 seconds.
- Every phone number and every out-of-date screen is gone.
- The end card turns the drawn mark into your real app icon above « Disponible sur l’App Store ».

It is buildable now from the takes already on disk, with no new recording.
notTaken: Day-in-the-salon's running clock (08:00 → 18:00). Not taken: the footage contradicts the chronology it asserts (the 08:00 booking already reads « Terminé », the revenue rows are dated 13 Oct, Yao K. appears twice), and two through-lines, the clock and the stroke, would compete. I kept its camera window cut at screen point 56, its walk-in copy and the tagline-next-to-the-logo rule. Its fixed-width digit cells are no longer needed, because there is no clock.

Day-in-the-salon's « Le total du jour, sans calculatrice. » (Revenus). Not taken: pro-08 and take3 show the pre-#592 label « Total », where the app now says « Total réalisé ». It is worth a beat only after recapturing Revenus « Aujourd’hui » on the current build.

Feature-rhythm's deposit drop « Exigez un acompte. / Payé sur votre Mobile Money. ». Not taken: no real screen exists, because the demo salon cannot pass KYC. Also, app-store-forms.md plans to hide KYC and deposits on iOS if Apple rejects under 5.1.1(ix), so an App-Store-only CTA could advertise something the iOS build does not show.

Feature-rhythm's five-verb kinetic montage with scale punch-ins and the Pro app-open M/W morph. Not taken: the verbs read like a generic feature list in a Paris-agency register, the punches are loud for a 'calm' brand, the phone at 46% makes the UI unreadable, and the morph needs a Lottie renderer the Python toolchain does not have. I kept its 0.5 s cut grid, the cover.png deliverable and its idea of naming the role in the hook.

Problem-solution's own « Encore un lapin ? » → « Chaque absence, notée sur sa fiche. » and its S8 three-still recap. Not taken: the only client file reads « 0 Absences », and a no-show pain next to a MyWeli screen implies a prevention the app does not deliver. The recap's stills went past the safe margin, and its untouched tagline headline had no logo near it.

Repeating the tagline on the end card, which both judges suggested as a second placement. Not taken: in 3.5 s the end card must give the CTA its full reading time, and growing the card would push brand time over 25%. The tagline appears once, beside the logo, in the first 5 s, and the post caption can carry it.
ownerQuestions: In Abidjan, does a salon owner say « carnet » or « cahier » for the paper appointment book? And do the four client messages (« C’est combien, les tresses ? », « Vous êtes où exactement ? », « Vous fermez à quelle heure ? », « Allô ? ») sound like what your clients really write?

There is no official « MyWeli Pro » lockup file. Do you approve the wordmark unit built from the MyWeli wordmark SVG plus the « Pro » letters of the Pro app-open animation? And do you approve the end card where the drawn mark becomes the Pro app icon?

Should we record one short re-take session on the current build before rendering? It would cover (a) the public page with « Voir les tarifs » opened, so prices show on the page itself, and (b) the walk-in booking under a name other than « Yao K. ». It writes one booking to the production demo salon. Or should we render now with the existing takes and the two caveats in the risks?

When will salons be able to go online so clients can find and book them? « Plus de clients » and the public-page beat assume that is live. Should posting wait for both the App Store release and the client-side launch?
